name: Question 13
problem:
Find the general solution of the following differential equation.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{x}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y}
$$
worked_solution:
This is a homogeneous equation because it is written in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y),
$$

and we notice that all terms in the numerator and denominator of $f(x,y)$ are of order $3$ (i.e., they are cubic).

Using the transformation $y=v(x)x$, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the differential equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y+{x}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{(vx)^{3}+x(vx)^{2}+{x}^{2}(vx)+{x}^{3}}{x(vx)^{2}+{x}^{2}(vx)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{x}^{3}({v}^{3}+{v}^{2}+v+1)}{{x}^{3}({v}^{2}+v)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{v}^{3}+{v}^{2}+v+1}{{v}^{2}+v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{v}^{3}+{v}^{2}+v+1}{{v}^{2}+v}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{v}^{3}+{v}^{2}+v+1-{v}^{3}-{v}^{2}}{{v}^{2}+v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v+1}{v(v+1)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{v} \\ v\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int v\,\text{d}v & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{v}^{2}}{2} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{2} & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{2} & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we introduced $C=2{C}_{1}.$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}\,.
$$

Finally, substituting the above into our solution, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\ {y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Find the general solution of the following differential equation. dydx=y3+xy2+x2y+x3xy2+x2y

a
y2=x2(ln⁡|x|)+C
b
y2=x2(−ln⁡|x|+C)
c
y2=x2(2ln⁡|x|+C)
d
y2=x(−2ln⁡|x|)+C
e
y2=x(ln⁡|x|+C)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

This is a homogeneous equation because it is written in the form

dydx=f(x,y),

and we notice that all terms in the numerator and denominator of f(x,y) are of order 3 (i.e., they are cubic).

Using the transformation y=v(x)x, we have: dydx=xdvdx+vddx(x)=xdvdx+v.

Substituting the above into the differential equation gives:

dydx=y3+xy2+x2y+x3xy2+x2yxdvdx+v=(vx)3+x(vx)2+x2(vx)+x3x(vx)2+x2(vx)xdvdx+v=x3(v3+v2+v+1)x3(v2+v)xdvdx+v=v3+v2+v+1v2+vxdvdx=v3+v2+v+1v2+v−vxdvdx=v3+v2+v+1−v3−v2v2+vxdvdx=v+1v(v+1)xdvdx=1vvdvdx=1x

Integrating both sides with respect to x, we obtain: ∫vdvdxdx=∫1xdx∫vdv=∫1xdxv22=ln⁡|x|+C1v2=2ln⁡|x|+2C1v2=2ln⁡|x|+C Notice that we introduced C=2C1.

From the transformation y=vx, we get v=yx. Finally, substituting the above into our solution, we obtain: y2x2=2ln⁡|x|+Cy2=x2(2ln⁡|x|+C)
